Blocked eCOCO (cross-fitted evolutionary correlation coefficient)

Source: R/ecoco_blocked.R
ecoco_blocked.Rd

Blocked eCOCO evaluates complete sliding validation windows with astronomical targets trained on strictly non-overlapping anchor windows. Four leakage-corrected orbital-group amplitudes (long eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession; groups identified by descending period rank) are fitted at regularly spaced anchor windows (spacing anchor_fraction * window) using the complete sedimentation-rate grid, and expanded to a coherent nine-term sine target. Every validation window is evaluated with the nearest lower-depth anchor (forward) and the nearest higher-depth anchor (backward) with frozen weights. The consensus correlation at a rate is the smaller of the two directional correlations; at the record edges the available direction is used (consensus_policy = "supported") or the window is left empty ("strict"). Stationary Gaussian AR(1) Monte Carlo nulls, one per unique window interval, repeat the complete anchor training and frozen validation. Global p-values use the null maximum over the complete rate grid within each window, local p-values the same rate. pCOCO = rho * |log10(p_global)| is the ridge score; the sedimentation-rate ridge is tracked as in Acycle (trackEcocoRidge). Translated from Acycle v3.1 ecocoCrossfitCore.m, ecoco.m (Blocked branch), ecocoWindowSpectra.m, ecocoEstimateAr1.m, ecocoPhysicalCenters.m, ecocoPhysicalWindowValues.m, cocoNonnegativeLeakageSolve.m and zeropad2.m (Mingsong Li). Uses the COCO helper functions of this package (helpers_coco.R and the ecoco_* functions).

Usage

ecoco_blocked(
  data = NULL,
  orbit9 = c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.682, 22.3758,
    18.9519),
  window = NULL,
  sr = NULL,
  step_depth = NULL,
  step = 1,
  pad = NULL,
  red = 0,
  n_sim = 2000,
  method = "Pearson",
  max_frequency = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  anchor_fraction = 0.5,
  window_mode = "physical-depth",
  edge_pad = TRUE,
  center_limits = NULL,
  compute_local_p = TRUE,
  consensus_policy = "supported",
  batch_size = 20,
  genplot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  centre_limits = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Record to analyse (matrix or data frame, two columns): depth in metres in column 1 and the proxy in column 2. Non-finite rows are dropped, duplicated depths averaged, and unevenly spaced data are linearly interpolated to the median sample spacing (see coco_prepare_regular_data). Required (Default=NULL).

orbit9

The nine astronomical target periods in kyr (numeric vector of nine distinct positive values: long eccentricity, four short eccentricity terms, obliquity, three precession terms), e.g. from orbit9_at_age for the age of the record. Default=c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.6820, 22.3758, 18.9519).

window

Length of the sliding validation and anchor windows, in metres (numeric, > 0; every window must contain at least 8 samples). NULL uses 25% of the record length (Acycle GUI default). Default=NULL.

sr

Sedimentation rates to test, in cm/kyr (numeric vector, > 0, strictly increasing). NULL uses the Acycle GUI default: from 2 * dt * 0.065 * 100 up to 100 cm/kyr (reduced so that the longest period fits in the record), in steps of 0.1 cm/kyr or at most 300 steps. Default=NULL.

step_depth

Spacing of the output (validation) window centres, in metres (numeric, > 0); only used with window_mode="physical-depth". NULL uses the sample interval dt, or dt * ceiling(n / 300) for more than 300 samples. Default=NULL.

step

Step between successive validation windows, in samples (integer, >= 1); only used with window_mode="legacy-count". Default=1.

pad

Length (number of points) to which every window is zero-padded for the periodogram (integer, at least the number of points per window). NULL uses the Acycle default: 5000 for up to 2500 samples, 10000 for up to 5000 samples, and floor(n / 5000) * 5000 + 5000 above that. Default=NULL.

red

Background (red-noise) removal applied to every window spectrum (integer): 0 none, 1 classical AR(1) background, 2 robust AR(1) background, 3 smoothed-window-average (SWA) background. Negative power after subtraction is set to zero. Default=0.

n_sim

Number of AR(1) Monte Carlo simulations used for the global and local p-values (integer, >= 0); each simulation repeats the anchor training and validation. Default=2000.

method

Correlation coefficient between the window spectrum and the target spectrum (character): "Pearson" or "Spearman". Default="Pearson".

max_frequency

Highest frequency of the target spectrum that enters the correlation, in cycles/kyr (numeric, at least max(1/orbit9)); NULL uses 1.2 * max(1/orbit9). Default=NULL.

seed

Seed of the random number generator (integer), so that the Monte Carlo results can be reproduced; NULL leaves the current random state unchanged. Default=1.

anchor_fraction

Spacing of the anchor windows (where the target amplitudes are trained) as a fraction of window (numeric, > 0 and <= 2); smaller values give more, overlapping anchors. Default=0.5.

window_mode

How the windows are defined (character): "physical-depth" (windows of fixed length in metres centred every step_depth, as in the Acycle wrapper and GUI) or "legacy-count" (windows of a fixed number of samples moved by step samples; needs evenly sampled data). Default="physical-depth".

edge_pad

Zero-pad the record by half a window at both ends and restrict the output centres to the original record, so that windows reach the record ends (logical, TRUE or FALSE; Acycle GUI setting for Blocked eCOCO). Only used with window_mode="physical-depth". Default=TRUE.

center_limits

Depths of the first and last output window centre, in metres (numeric vector c(first, last), or NULL); overrides the limits set by edge_pad. NULL uses the record ends (with edge_pad=TRUE) or c(first depth + window/2, last depth - window/2). Default=NULL.

compute_local_p

Also compute the local p-values, comparing each rate with the null correlations at the same rate (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

consensus_policy

How windows at the record edges, which have an anchor on only one side, are treated (character): "supported" uses the available direction, "strict" leaves windows without both a forward and a backward anchor empty. Default="supported".

batch_size

Number of Monte Carlo simulations processed together (integer, >= 1); larger batches are faster but use more memory, the results do not depend on it. Default=20.

genplot

Plot the result with plot_ecoco_cv (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

verbose

Print progress messages (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

centre_limits

British spelling of center_limits; if given (not NULL) it overrides center_limits. Default=NULL.

Value

A list (class "ecoco_cv") with elements method, sr (rate grid), depth (window centres), rate-by-window matrices rho, p_global, p_local, norbit, pcoco and score (the published consensus surface), the lists forward, backward, consensus, strict (each with rho, p_global, p_local, norbit, pcoco, best_rate, ...), support (per-window "bidirectional", "forward-only", "backward-only" or "none"), windows and anchors (data frames with bounds, anchor links and trained rates/weights), geometry (rate masks), rho_m (per-window AR(1)), best (best rate per window) and track (tracked ridge: depth, sr, rho, p_global, norbit, score, sr_low, sr_high).

References

Li, M., Kump, L.R., Hinnov, L.A., Mann, M.E., 2018. Tracking variable sedimentation rates and astronomical forcing in Phanerozoic paleoclimate proxy series with evolutionary correlation coefficients and hypothesis testing. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 501, 165-179. doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2018.08.041

Li, M., Hinnov, L., Kump, L., 2019. Acycle: Time-series analysis software for paleoclimate research and education. Computers & Geosciences 127, 12-22. doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2019.02.011

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
dt <- 0.05
depth <- seq(0, 30, by = dt)
tt <- depth * 100 / 5          # 5 cm/kyr
x <- sin(2 * pi * tt / 405.7) + 0.8 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 98.9) +
  0.5 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 40.99) + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 23.68) +
  0.3 * rnorm(length(tt))
res <- ecoco_blocked(cbind(depth, x), window = 10, sr = seq(3, 8, 0.5),
                     step_depth = 1, pad = 400, n_sim = 20)
#> Warning: Blocked eCOCO has no tested rate with complete all-nine training geometry; continuing with the partial-orbit target at 8 of 11 rates (degraded/exploratory result).
